nd3f74ee9998.s: Inscriptions giving dates and the names of sculptors are among the notable firsts of which dynasty?
nd3f74ee9998.x: Dated inscriptions naming sculptors are listed among the Ikshvaku firsts, along with early Hindu temples such as Pushpabhadraswami and Ashtabhuja Narayana at Nagarjunakonda.

n78ec40c44da.s: An Ashvamedha platform corroborating the Vedic sacrifices of Vasishthiputra Chamtamula has been found at:
n78ec40c44da.x: Chamtamula performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and Rajasuya; the Ashvamedha platform at Nagarjunakonda is the evidence.

n78136c07e20.s: Which historian derives the name 'Ikshvaku' from ikshu (sugarcane)?
n78136c07e20.x: B.S.L. Hanumantha Rao links the name Ikshvaku to ikshu, sugarcane.

n44bcd94b3ef.s: The first Sanskrit inscriptions in the Telugu lands belong to the reign of:
n44bcd94b3ef.x: Ehuvala Chamtamula, son of Virapurushadatta, issued the first Sanskrit inscriptions in the Telugu lands; the Gummadidurru inscription is also his.

nab247808c4f.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates)
nab247808c4f.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and Agnistoma sacrifices?
nab247808c4f.x: Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and Agnistoma; an Ashvamedha altar has been found at Nagarjunakonda.

n8156281534b.s: Under the Ikshvakus, which varna constituted the majority of society?
n8156281534b.x: Shudras were the majority under the Ikshvakus, while Brahmins benefited from Brahmadeya grants and a new landlord class emerged.

ne99dd9657fd.s: The inscriptions of Ikshvaku royal women show that their donations to Buddhism were made:
ne99dd9657fd.x: While the kings were Vedic, queens and royal women were major patrons of Buddhism, and their inscriptions record donations made without male intervention.

nb69aab8831f.s: Ikshvaku marriage alliances linked them with the Kshatrapas of Ujjain and the:
nb69aab8831f.x: Ikshvaku marriage alliances linked them with the Kshatrapas of Ujjain and the Chutus; cross-cousin marriage also began with them.

n129fdb5213a.s: The naming of Ehuvala Santamula after his grandfather is a social practice recorded in the inscriptions of the:
n129fdb5213a.x: Ikshvaku inscriptions record names derived from the grandfather (Ehuvala Santamula), matronymics such as Vasishthiputra, and sati.

n1214eaf273c.s: Ikshvaku coins were mainly made of:
n1214eaf273c.x: Ikshvaku coins were of lead and copper and bore the Ujjain symbol, the elephant and the lion; they are found in Guntur, Krishna and Godavari districts.

n9a39d7b6e72.s: Chamtisri built or restored the Maha Chaitya at Nagarjunakonda in which regnal year of Virapurushadatta?
n9a39d7b6e72.x: Chamtisri, sister of Sri Santamula and paternal aunt of Virapurushadatta, built or restored the Maha Chaitya in his sixth regnal year.

n2521272ddbc.s: Upasika Bodhisri, ranked first among women donors at Nagarjunakonda, was the daughter of Revanta of:
n2521272ddbc.x: Bodhisri was a non-royal donor, the daughter of Revanta of Amaravati; Chamtisri is regarded as the first woman donor.

n5af19849967.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no clear dates)
n5af19849967.s: The Paravata Mahachaitya, later rebuilt by Chamtisri, had earlier been built for Acharya Nagarjuna by:
n5af19849967.x: The earlier Paravata Mahachaitya was built by Yajnasri Satakarni for Acharya Nagarjuna; Chamtisri rebuilt it in Virapurushadatta's sixth year with nine Ayaka pillars.

n5fa0a940e5c.s: Ehuvala Santamula built a vihara in his mother's name for which Buddhist sect?
n5fa0a940e5c.x: Ehuvala Santamula, who revived Brahmanism, also continued Buddhist patronage by building a vihara for the Bahushrutiyas in his mother's name.

n97337a33aa2.s: Bodhisri's Sinhala Vihara at Nagarjunakonda belonged to which sect?
n97337a33aa2.x: Bodhisri's Sinhala Vihara belonged to the Mahaviharavasins; the Maha Chaitya was Aparamahavinaseliya and Kodabalisri's vihara Mahishasaka.

nap-history-7-17.s: Who was the tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus?
nap-history-7-17.x: Hariti was the tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus; Kumara Swami was the deity of commander Elisiri's temple.

n744b035ac5e.s: The Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami temple at Nagarjunakonda was built by Shivasena, commander of the Abhira king:
n744b035ac5e.x: Shivasena, commander of the Abhira king Vasusena, built the Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami, the first Vaishnava temple in Andhra.

nba18efe93ea.s: Besides one Vaishnava temple, how many Shaiva temples stood at Nagarjunakonda?
nba18efe93ea.x: Nine Shaiva temples and one Vaishnava temple (Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami) stood at Nagarjunakonda.

n8406c1e2b06.s: The installation of the image of Hariti in the Ikshvaku period marks the beginning of:
n8406c1e2b06.x: Hariti, tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus and protector of children, marks the beginning of Shakti worship, not Vaishnava worship.

n2bc5eca95db.s: Which Ikshvaku king granted agraharas to Brahmins from the north?
n2bc5eca95db.x: Sri Santamula worshipped Virupakshapati and Mahasena and granted agraharas to northern Brahmins.

n00c42f24304.s: The Pushpabhadraswami shrine at Nagarjunakonda followed which plan?
n00c42f24304.x: The Shaiva Pushpabhadraswami shrine had a Gajaprishtha or elephant-back plan; it was begun by Virapurushadatta and completed by Ehuvala.

n167f21db7da.s: Upasika Bodhisri built seven viharas at:
n167f21db7da.x: Bodhisri built seven viharas at Papili and viharas for monks from Sinhala, Kashmir, China and Gandhara.

ne230abcd224.s: Sriparvataswami, the family deity of the Vishnukundins, is identified with:
ne230abcd224.x: Sriparvataswami, the family deity of the Vishnukundins, is identified with Srisaila Mallikarjuna.

nap-history-7-15.s: The Pedavegi inscription recording a land grant to Vishnu belongs to the Salankayana king:
nap-history-7-15.x: The Pedavegi inscription of the Salankayana king Nandivarman II records a land grant to Vishnu.

nap-history-6-18.s: The Harati, Mahajana, Kumara Swami and Pushpabhadra Swami temples were discovered in the excavations at:
nap-history-6-18.x: Harati, Mahajana, Kumara Swami, Pushpabhadra Swami and Ashtabhuja Narayana Swami are temples found in the Nagarjunakonda excavations.

nap-history-7-3.s: The Salankayanas called themselves devotees of Bappa Bhattaraka, a term meaning:
nap-history-7-3.x: The Salankayanas were devotees of Bappa Bhattaraka, a term meaning consideration of the father as God.

na0c185edbe2.s: The last royal Buddhist zenith in Andhra was under the:
na0c185edbe2.x: The Ikshvakus represented the last royal Buddhist zenith in Andhra; their period also saw the first Vaishnava temple, Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami.

ne00334b5cfc.shape: one-liner (match not possible: the original confirms too few pairs)
ne00334b5cfc.s: Nagarjunakonda was a main centre of which school of sculpture?
ne00334b5cfc.x: Nagarjunakonda was a main centre of the Amaravati School, which reached its final, mature phase with Mahayana themes under the Ikshvakus.

nca00aa38928.s: The Mandhata sculpture, the first depiction of a Chakravarti in Indian art, is found at:
nca00aa38928.x: The Mandhata sculpture at Jaggayyapeta, the most important Ikshvaku sculpture, is the first depiction of a Chakravarti.

nd9314b15ab5.s: Early Ikshvaku carving is called the 'last flicker' of which tradition?
nd9314b15ab5.x: Early Ikshvaku carving, with less stylisation and low relief, is called the 'last flicker' of the Satavahana Amaravati tradition.

n6999aacb516.s: The first sculptor signatures and the first Sanskrit inscription in South India are associated with the:
n6999aacb516.x: The Ikshvakus are associated with the first sculptor signatures, the first Sanskrit inscription in South India and the first structural Hindu temples.

n1a05d14422c.x: Ayaka platforms belong to stupas; the Agamic temple plan has garbhagudi, antarala, mantapa, dhvajastambha and prakara.

n79c6ca08531.s: The major stupas at Nagarjunakonda were built on which plan?
n79c6ca08531.x: The major stupas at Nagarjunakonda had a wheel-shaped, spoked plan with Ayaka platforms in the four directions.

n07e82514502.s: Indrapalanagara, the early Vishnukundin capital, is identified with:
n07e82514502.x: Indrapalanagara (Sukrapuram), built by Indravarma and the capital of Madhava Varma I and Govinda Varma, is Tummalagudem in Telangana.

n9c10ed05247.s: Which is regarded as the first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana?
n9c10ed05247.x: The Tummalagudem plates, associated with Govinda Varma I, are regarded as the first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana.

nd160775e0a7.s: In which year did Pulakeshin II defeat Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala (Kolleru), ending Vishnukundin rule?
nd160775e0a7.x: Pulakeshin II ended Vishnukundin rule at Kunala near Kolleru in 624 CE; his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana then founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.

ncd2f6273412.s: Govinda Varma's Chaitanyapuri inscription was written in:
ncd2f6273412.x: Of the 21 Vishnukundin inscriptions, Govinda Varma's Chaitanyapuri record was in Prakrit, so not all were in Sanskrit.

n371c56506c3.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler bore the title Satyasraya?
n371c56506c3.x: Indrabhattaraka Varma bore the title Satyasraya; Govinda Varma was Shadabhigna and Vikramendra Varma I was Mahakavi.

n0f03bef60eb.s: The Chikkulla plates, containing the Telugu phrase 'Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul', belong to:
n0f03bef60eb.x: The Chikkulla plates (Tuni, East Godavari) are of Vikramendra Varma II and carry the Telugu phrase 'Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul'.

n02658bdf7a2.s: The Vishnukundin ruler Indrabhattaraka Varma was defeated by the Maukhari king:
n02658bdf7a2.x: Indrabhattaraka Varma was defeated by Maukhari Ishanavarma and was killed in the Kalinga war.

nc2dc66b2ca4.s: The Salankayanas of Vengi were conquered by which Vishnukundin ruler?
nc2dc66b2ca4.x: Madhava Varma II conquered the Vaishnava Salankayanas, whose capital was Vengi (Pedavegi in Eluru district).

n59faf74a300.s: For how many years did Madhava Varma I rule?
n59faf74a300.x: Madhava Varma I ruled for 22 years, married a Vakataka princess and is associated with the Undavalli, Bhairavakona and Mogalrajapuram caves.

n5f990147e27.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates)
n5f990147e27.s: The Paramabhattarika Mahadevi Vihara was founded by the queen of:
n5f990147e27.x: The queen of Govinda Varma I founded the Paramabhattarika Mahadevi Vihara; Govinda Varma I himself founded the Govinda Vihara.

n8dc060b89d8.s: Under the Vishnukundins, the tax called Bhaga represented what share of the produce?
n8dc060b89d8.x: Bhaga was one-sixth of the produce; Vishti was forced labour, later called vetti in Telugu.

n0e0b240778e.s: The Vishnukundin Tundi plates record the grant of Tundi village to the scholar:
n0e0b240778e.x: The Tundi plates record the grant of Tundi village to Shivavarma; the Ipur plates name Agnisarma and Easwarasarma, and Mutukali went to Indravarma and Agnivarma.

n4eb14750e0d.s: Janasraya Chhandovichiti, associated with Madhava Varma II, is a Sanskrit work on:
n4eb14750e0d.x: Janasraya Chhandovichiti is a Sanskrit work on prosody, credited to Madhava Varma II (title Janasraya) or to the poet Gunaswami writing in his name.

o: iron with a thin copper coating
n1c104c774a6.x: Vishnukundin coins were of iron with a thin copper coating (APPSC GS 2018 key); Rayaprolu Subrahmanyam brought them to light.

n13bb487ec76.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Undavalli caves?
o: They are situated in Guntur district.
They are situated on the bank of the Godavari.
Their architecture is a Vishnukundina adaptation of the Gupta rock-cut style.
They contain a five-metre reclining image of Ananta Padmanabha Vishnu.
n13bb487ec76.x: The Undavalli caves are on the Krishna in Guntur district, not on the Godavari; the other three statements are correct.

nb4d7ba66987.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates)
nb4d7ba66987.s: How many rock-cut caves are there at Bhairavakonda?
nb4d7ba66987.x: Bhairavakonda, a Kapalika Shaiva centre, has eight rock-cut caves; 4, 9 and 12 are the usual traps.

ndff0a54ef4c.s: The Undavalli caves contain a monolithic reclining statue of:
ndff0a54ef4c.x: Undavalli, a Vishnukundin cave of the 4th-5th c. CE on the Krishna, contains a monolithic reclining Ananta Padmanabha Swamy.

n40eef71c738.s: The rock-cut caves of the Pallava king Mahendravarman I are dated to the:
n40eef71c738.x: Mahendravarman I's caves belong to the 7th century, while the Vishnukundin caves are generally dated to the 4th-6th centuries.

na500ce61b1a.s: Some sources credit the Bhairavakonda caves to which Vishnukundin ruler?
na500ce61b1a.x: APP and CDX credit Madhava Varma I, while APHQ dates the caves to the Pallava period of the 7th-8th centuries CE.

nb6e7d0f17d0.s: The Undavalli caves were first used as a/an:
nb6e7d0f17d0.x: Undavalli was first a Jain abode, then used by Buddhist monks, and later converted into a Hindu temple.

n77e09d0cad6.s: How many storeys do the Undavalli caves have?
n77e09d0cad6.x: Undavalli has four storeys with three main caves; it was carved top-down, with finely detailed upper levels and a crude ground floor.

n24e1d6493c1.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates)
n24e1d6493c1.s: The offspring of a Viloma (Pratiloma) union was termed:
n24e1d6493c1.x: Viloma, a lower-caste man with a higher-caste woman, produced offspring termed Chandala; Anuloma offspring were termed Ugra.

nap-history-45-17.s: Samayamu were caste associations during the rule of the:
nap-history-45-17.x: Samayamu were caste associations of the Kakatiya period; Kayasthas were record-keepers.

nc875e20718f.s: The amphitheatre at Nagarjunakonda, the Ikshvaku capital Vijayapuri, was used mainly for:
nc875e20718f.x: The Nagarjunakonda amphitheatre was for performances and games, not Vedic sacrifices.

nfb3da07bd6a.s: Which Satavahana-period inscription refers to Brahmins trained in Vedic learning and rituals?
nfb3da07bd6a.x: The Nanaghat inscription mentions Brahmins trained in Vedic learning and ritual; Satavahana kings enforced varna-dharma and granted tax-free villages to Brahmins.

nf3c52a1d5ce.s: In early Andhra society, the Selavaddikas were:
nf3c52a1d5ce.x: Selavaddikas were stone sculptors or masons; Halikas were farmers, Sethis merchants and Swarnakaras goldsmiths.

na70fe75486c.s: Under the Vishnukundins, which group was regarded as 'the backbone' of society and received land grants?
na70fe75486c.x: Farmers were 'the backbone' and received land grants; Vaisyas carried on trade, and Sudras such as carpenters and weavers had a recognised place.

n45770835f85.s: Along with Paramamaheswara, the Vishnukundins bore the title:
n45770835f85.x: The Vishnukundins, whose family deity was Sriparvataswamy, bore the titles Paramamaheswara and Parama Brahmanya.

n8c6a16316b0.s: Which literary work mentions inter-caste marriages, showing that caste was not completely rigid in the early period?
n8c6a16316b0.x: Kathasaritsagara mentions inter-caste marriages, showing that caste practices were not completely rigid at that stage.

n40a7f06e78b.s: In the Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda reliefs, men are shown wearing a lower cloth and a:
n40a7f06e78b.x: The reliefs show men in a lower cloth and turban, and women with heavy anklets, bangles, girdles and necklaces.

n912cd994fcd.s: Unlike the Ikshvaku queens, who patronised Buddhism, the Ikshvaku kings performed:
n912cd994fcd.x: Ikshvaku kings performed Vedic sacrifices, whereas Ikshvaku queens patronised Buddhism.

nfad55407200.s: The Satavahana royal woman Gautami Balasri funded a cave-vihara at:
nfad55407200.x: Gautami Balasri, a Satavahana woman patron, funded a cave-vihara at Nasik; she is not among the Gathasaptasati poets.

n6b0c1bd0889.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sangam corpus?
o: Pathinenkilkanakku is older than Ettuthogai and Pattupattu.
n6b0c1bd0889.x: Pathinenkilkanakku, the eighteen minor works on ethics, is largely post-Sangam, so it is not older than Ettuthogai and Pattupattu (the Melkanakku).

na9ce97f1650.s: According to tradition, the second Sangam was held at:
na9ce97f1650.x: Tradition places the first Sangam at Then Madurai, the second at Kapatapuram and the third at Madurai, all under Pandya patronage.

ndcacda52711.s: The Sangams, assemblies of Tamil poets, were held under the patronage of the:
ndcacda52711.x: The Sangams were held under Pandya patronage, not Chola; the corpus has about 2,400 poems.

n93c91dd601f.s: Ettuthogai and Pattupattu poems are divided into aham and:
n93c91dd601f.x: Ettuthogai and Pattupattu are divided into aham and puram themes.

n9d0a5b4e3cb.s: In the Tirukkural, the book Porul deals with:
n9d0a5b4e3cb.x: The Tirukkural's 1,330 couplets are in three books: Aram (virtue), Porul (wealth) and Inbam (love).

ncde45732ad2.s: Sangam literature was composed in Tamil, while the contemporary Satavahanas used:
ncde45732ad2.x: Tamil was the language of Sangam literature, while the contemporary Satavahanas used Prakrit.

nindian-history-13-4.s: The oldest extant Tamil grammar is the:
nindian-history-13-4.x: Tolkappiyam, which deals with grammar and poetics, is the oldest extant Tamil grammar.

n8b7eb8b6d7a.s: Which of the following belongs to the Ettuthogai (eight anthologies)?
n8b7eb8b6d7a.x: Padirruppattu, on the Chera kings, is one of the Ettuthogai; Pattinappalai, Mullaippattu and Tirumurugarruppadai belong to Pattupattu.

n0a3792c63f9.s: Manimekalai tells how the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi became a:
n0a3792c63f9.x: Manimekalai relates how the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi becomes a Buddhist nun and reflects Buddhist philosophy.

ndf55074cfde.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates)
ndf55074cfde.s: Which Chola ruler, victor at Venni and Vahaipparandalai, is the subject of Pattinappalai?
ndf55074cfde.x: Karikala Chola won the battles of Venni and Vahaipparandalai, reclaimed forest land and is associated with Pattinappalai.

ne593c7eb791.s: In Sangam polity, the minor hill and forest chieftains were called:
ne593c7eb791.x: Minor hill and forest chieftains were the Velir; Enadi was a title of army commanders and Avai the royal court.

nindian-history-15-11.s: Naura, Tondi, Mushiri (Muziris) and Nelisanda were major Sangam-age ports on the:
o: western coast, mainly in the Chera country
eastern coast, mainly in the Chola country
nindian-history-15-11.x: All four were major western-coast ports of the Sangam age, mainly in the Chera country.

n6a77562d075.s: Pari, Kari, Ori, Pegan, Ay, Athiyaman and Nalli are collectively known as the:
n6a77562d075.x: These seven were the great patrons, the Kadai ezhu vallals; Nedunjeliyan, a Pandya ruler, was not among them.

nd80a221db0a.s: Korkai was the port of which Sangam kingdom?
nd80a221db0a.x: Korkai was the Pandya port; the Chola port was Kaveripattinam (Puhar), with the capital at Uraiyur.

n91cf90e6d8c.s: In the Sangam age, Nalli was one of the:
n91cf90e6d8c.x: Nalli was one of the seven great patrons, not a minister of the Aimperunkulu.

n63e3cb34d67.s: The Pallavas, who were not a Sangam dynasty, rose from which century CE?
n63e3cb34d67.x: The Pallavas rose from the fourth century CE; the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas were the three Sangam dynasties.

n5c61922e949.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates)
n5c61922e949.s: In the Sangam tradition, hero stones set up for warriors who fell in battle were called:
n5c61922e949.x: Nadukal were set up for fallen warriors, could carry carvings of their deeds and inscriptions, and were found across Tamil Nadu.

n1e26a3db65e.s: Indo-Roman trade in the southern peninsula reached its peak during the:
n1e26a3db65e.x: Indo-Roman trade peaked in the Satavahana-Sangam age, broadly 1st century BCE to 2nd century CE, and declined after the Satavahanas.

n291f22eebd0.s: In the Tolkappiyam's list of four castes, which group stands fourth?
n291f22eebd0.x: The Tolkappiyam lists Arasar, Anthanar, Vanigar and Vellalar, with Vellalar fourth.

nc0dc6cc63a0.s: Arikamedu, the foremost Indo-Roman trading station on the east coast, was excavated by Mortimer Wheeler in:
nc0dc6cc63a0.x: Wheeler excavated Arikamedu, near Puducherry, in 1945; finds include Roman amphorae, Arretine ware and rouletted ware.

naf96318908d.s: The rule of which dynasty is often called the 'dark age' of Tamil history?
naf96318908d.x: The Kalabhra period was called a dark age because later Brahmanical records portrayed them as evil and sources are scarce.

n2cd07440107.s: In Indo-Roman trade, Yavanapriya ('beloved of the Yavanas') referred to:
n2cd07440107.x: Yavanapriya meant black pepper, Rome's most prized Indian import; muslin and ivory were exports and sweet wine an import.

n7f3f2b8457a.s: Which of the following was a woman poet of the Sangam age?
n7f3f2b8457a.x: Women poets such as Avvaiyar, Nachchellaiyar and Kakkaipadiniyar contributed to Sangam poetry.

nindian-history-26-2-12.s: Muziris (Mushiri) was the chief port of the:
nindian-history-26-2-12.x: Muziris was the chief Chera port; Korkai was Pandya, Puhar Chola and Motupalli Kakatiya.

nindian-history-26-13.s: Motupalli, known for its trade inscription, was a port of the:
nindian-history-26-13.x: Motupalli was a Kakatiya port in Andhra, whereas Puhar (Kaveripattinam) was the major Chola port.

n38b754e5ed8.x: The Kalabhras are described as patrons of Jainism and Buddhism rather than Vedic Brahmanism.

n6007567edc9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Samudragupta's campaigns?
o: The Ganga-Yamuna region was directly annexed.
Assam, Nepal and Bengal were frontier rulers who paid tribute.
The southern kingdoms were permanently annexed.
The atavika (forest) kingdoms of central India were subdued.
n6007567edc9.x: The southern rulers were defeated and reinstated as tributaries, not permanently annexed; the other three are correct.

n226e3e7cf0f.s: Meghavarman of Sri Lanka sent a mission to Samudragupta to build a monastery at:
n226e3e7cf0f.x: Meghavarman's request to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya is known from a Chinese source.

n8d2e079960d.s: Who called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India'?
n8d2e079960d.x: V.A. Smith called Samudragupta the Napoleon of India; the Allahabad prashasti calls him Lichchhavi-dauhitra.

n59ff2b8bb02.s: Samudragupta's policy towards the twelve defeated southern kings was:
n59ff2b8bb02.x: The twelve southern kings were captured, released and reinstated (grahana-moksha-anugraha); there was no permanent annexation in the south.

nindian-history-1-15.s: Which Gupta record describes Skandagupta's war with the Hunas?
nindian-history-1-15.x: The Bhitari Pillar records Skandagupta's war with the Hunas; Eran gives the first evidence of sati and Mehrauli names Chandra.

n8ecd9eb68ab.s: Who wrote both the Mudrarakshasa and the Devichandraguptam?
n8ecd9eb68ab.x: Vishakhadatta wrote both plays; the Devichandraguptam tells the Ramagupta-Dhruvadevi-Chandragupta II story.

nb97a61be215.x: Kuberanaga was the queen of Chandragupta II; Kumaradevi, Duttadevi and Anantadevi were queens of Chandragupta I, Samudragupta and Kumaragupta I.

nd342e0d7679.s: Harisena of Samudragupta's court held the offices of Kumaramatya, Mahadandanayaka and:
nd342e0d7679.x: Harisena was Kumaramatya, Sandhivigrahika and Mahadandanayaka; he is not to be confused with the later Jain author of the Brihatkatha Kosha.

nbd705251bd5.s: The Mandsaur inscription is associated with:
nbd705251bd5.x: Vatsabhatti is linked with the Mandsaur inscription; Virasena with Udayagiri.

n90ffa1da7fc.s: The first Gupta ruler to assume the title 'Maharajadhiraja' was:
n90ffa1da7fc.x: Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha used 'Maharaja'; Chandragupta I was the first to assume 'Maharajadhiraja'.

nindian-history-1-70.s: Harisena's Prayag Prashasti was written in Sanskrit in which script?
nindian-history-1-70.x: Harisena wrote the Prayag Prashasti in Sanskrit, in Brahmi script, as a panegyric of Samudragupta.

nb06372e42c0.s: Who issued the first Gupta gold coins of the king-queen type?
nb06372e42c0.x: Chandragupta I, who married the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi, issued the first Gupta gold coins of the king-queen type.

nbeab6c71d21.s: According to Gupta records, which powers paid homage to the Gupta ruler?
nbeab6c71d21.x: Kushanas and Sakas paid homage, while kings of Southeast Asia and Ceylon sent tribute.

n711254a78c5.s: The Allahabad Prasasti of Samudragupta mixes prose and verse in which style?
n711254a78c5.x: The Allahabad (Prayaga) Prasasti is a Sanskrit eulogy in the champu style, mixing prose and verse.

n83962efb74b.s: The capital of Chandragupta I was:
n83962efb74b.x: Chandragupta I ruled South Bihar and parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Saketa and Prayaga, with Pataliputra as capital.

n7d016cbcd2f.s: Most Gupta coins, which reveal royal titles, religion and prosperity, were made of:
n7d016cbcd2f.x: Gupta coins were mostly gold and depict rulers, deities and rituals.

nindian-history-1-35.s: The Eran inscription, the first epigraphic evidence of sati, records the sati of the wife of the commander:
nindian-history-1-35.x: The Eran inscription of 510 AD records that the wife of the commander Goparaja burned herself on his pyre.

nindian-history-82-4.s: Which Mauryan ruler extended Mauryan power into the Deccan?
nindian-history-82-4.x: Bindusara pushed Mauryan power into the Deccan; Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire.

nindian-history-82-5.x: Kumaragupta I founded Nalanda; Harsha patronised Banabhatta and Skandagupta resisted the Hunas.

ne1d1afc3e15.s: Gupta land grants contributed to the empire's decline by encouraging the growth of:
ne1d1afc3e15.x: Land grants encouraged feudatories, and hereditary governors grew into autonomous feudatories rather than strengthening central control.

nd4fefb7c891.s: The last ruler of the main Gupta line was:
nd4fefb7c891.x: Vishnugupta, ruling c. 540-550 CE, was the last of the main Gupta line.

n768bf94cfa1.s: The Maitrakas, a successor power of the Guptas, ruled from:
n768bf94cfa1.x: The Maitrakas were at Valabhi; the Aulikaras at Mandsaur, the Pushyabhutis at Thanesar and the Later Guptas in Magadha.

ndac6a5af14c.s: In the Ramagupta episode, the queen whom Ramagupta agreed to surrender to a Saka king was:
ndac6a5af14c.x: Ramagupta agreed to surrender Dhruvadevi; Chandragupta II killed the Saka king and Ramagupta and married her.

n2760f3d89bb.s: Chandragupta II annexed western Malwa and Gujarat by defeating the Saka ruler:
n2760f3d89bb.x: Chandragupta II defeated Rudrasimha III, annexed western Malwa and Gujarat and made Ujjain his second capital.

nindian-history-96-1.s: The Gupta era (319-20 CE) was started by:
nindian-history-96-1.x: Chandragupta I started the Gupta era in 319-20 CE.

n0a203d808f8.s: Which Gupta ruler repulsed the Hunas twice?
n0a203d808f8.x: Skandagupta repulsed the Hunas twice and took the title Vikramaditya.

naa35a5758d8.s: Besides Mahendraditya, Kumaragupta I bore the title:
naa35a5758d8.x: Kumaragupta I was Shakraditya and Mahendraditya; Vikramaditya belongs to Chandragupta II and Skandagupta.

n754604f1dad.s: Chandragupta II was also known as Devaraja and:
n754604f1dad.x: Chandragupta II was also called Devagupta and Devaraja; Baladitya was Narasimhagupta.

n53954e031d1.s: Chandragupta II's daughter Prabhavati Gupta married the Vakataka ruler:
n53954e031d1.x: Prabhavati Gupta married Rudrasena II; the alliance extended Gupta influence into the Deccan without direct annexation.

ne2a70eb8f2d.s: In the later Gupta period, land grants weakened the state's ability to keep a professional army by reducing its:
ne2a70eb8f2d.x: Land grants reduced the revenue available to the state, which weakened its ability to maintain a professional army.

nindian-history-97-4.s: Chandragupta II's title Vikramaditya is linked with his victory over the:
nindian-history-97-4.x: Chandragupta II took the title Vikramaditya, linked with his victory over the Sakas.

n63d44dacd61.s: Which of the following was a major successor power of the Guptas in the north and west?
n63d44dacd61.x: The Maukharis, Maitrakas and Pushyabhutis were Gupta successor powers; the Paramaras of Malwa were a later power.

n592332812fd.s: Which invasion is identified as a cause of the decline of the Gupta Empire?
n592332812fd.x: Huna invasions, growth of feudatories and loss of western trade revenue were causes of Gupta decline; the Arab invasion was not.

nd410c2dccc6.s: Which Gupta ruler reinstated some defeated rulers as feudatories?
nd410c2dccc6.x: Samudragupta reinstated some feudatories; the Gupta Empire relied on feudatories and grantees and was less centralised than the Mauryan.

nfa001226b18.s: In the Gupta period, devagrahara grants were made to:
nfa001226b18.x: Devagrahara was assigned to temples and monasteries; brahmadeya and agrahara went to Brahmanas and secular grants to officials or feudatories.

n94220cb3cb4.s: In the Gupta land classification, Khila meant:
n94220cb3cb4.x: Khila was untilled waste land; Kshetra was cultivated land, Vastu house-site land and Aprahata uncultivated forest land.

nff48b96401b.s: In the Gupta judicial system, disputes relating to property were treated as:
nff48b96401b.x: The Gupta period separated civil and criminal law more clearly: theft and adultery were criminal, property disputes civil.

ne043e83ef18.s: Tribal groups absorbed into the caste order through Gupta-era land grants could emerge as new:
ne043e83ef18.x: Land grants in forest frontiers brought virgin land under cultivation and absorbed tribes into the caste order as new sub-castes.

naf694b4e294.s: Compared with the centrally regulated Mauryan state, Gupta administration relied more on:
naf694b4e294.x: The Mauryan state was centrally regulated, whereas Gupta administration relied to a greater extent on feudatories and grantees.

nb97d6646a4a.s: In the Gupta period, peasants increasingly became:
nb97d6646a4a.x: Peasants became semi-servile, bound by tenant farming, sharecropping, tenancy at will and many taxes.

n9fd8d335dca.s: On the Gupta town board (adhikarana), the Prathama kulika represented the:
n9fd8d335dca.x: The Prathama kulika represented the chief artisans; the Nagarashreshthi chaired the board, the Prathama kayastha was chief scribe and the Sarthavaha the caravan trader.

nindian-history-83-14.s: In ancient Indian revenue terms, Hiranya was:
o: a cash payment instead of produce
nindian-history-83-14.x: Hiranya was a cash payment; Bhaga was the share of produce, Valiam a commodity tax and Sita revenue from crown land.

nindian-history-23-3.s: In the Gupta period, Vishti, counted as a source of state income, meant:
nindian-history-23-3.x: Vishti was forced labour and was treated as a form of tax; tax-free land went to Brahmins and religious functionaries.

n9b79a8b5f7b.s: Satavahana and Ikshvaku brahmadeya grants barred whom from interfering in the granted areas?
n9b79a8b5f7b.x: Brahmadeya grants of the Satavahanas and Ikshvakus barred royal officials from interfering in the granted areas.

n4bdd79d558d.s: Under the Gupta kings, salaries of officials were often paid in:
n4bdd79d558d.x: Gupta kingship was hereditary without firm primogeniture; several offices were hereditary and salaries were often paid in land or kind.

nd4d35876cba.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about society as described by Fa-Hien?
o: Chandalas followed the same food restrictions as everyone else.
Cowrie shells were used in daily exchange.
Hindus and Buddhists lived in harmony.
The people were peaceful and prosperous.
nd4d35876cba.x: The Chandalas were an exception to the general food restrictions; the other three are Fa-Hien's observations.

n46ad554529b.s: Regarding marriage of girls, the Gupta-period Dharmashastras advocated:
n46ad554529b.x: The Dharmashastras advocated pre-puberty marriage; widows were to remain celibate, svayamvara gave way to arranged marriages and women were generally denied education.

neb07cba5bfd.s: Which was the largest west-coast port in the Gupta period?
neb07cba5bfd.x: Bharuch was the largest west-coast port; Tamralipti was an eastern port and Ghantasala and Kadura were in Krishna district.

n1f9dbcedc45.s: In Gupta times, ordinary daily exchange was carried on mainly with:
n1f9dbcedc45.x: Cowries were used in ordinary exchange; copper issues were few and later dinaras contained less gold.

n2e0ff11e3ee.s: The Indore copper plate records an endowment with which guild for maintaining a temple lamp?
n2e0ff11e3ee.x: The Indore plate concerns the oil-men's guild and a temple lamp; the Dashpur inscription concerns the silk-weavers' guild and the Damodarpur plates guild banking.

ncdc23c81924.s: The silk-weavers' guild of the Mandsaur (Dashpur) inscription migrated to Dashpur from:
ncdc23c81924.x: The guild came from Lata in Gujarat and built a Sun temple at Dashpur; weavers changing profession point to falling silk demand.

n7b19ac907a7.s: The decline of trade in North India was partly caused by the collapse of the:
n7b19ac907a7.x: The collapse of the West Roman Empire, the decline of the Sassanids and Huna disruption of the north-western route caused the decline.

n37633425890.s: Sopara, a major Gupta-era centre of trade with Rome and South-East Asia, lay in:
n37633425890.x: Sopara and Barbaricum were in western India; Pratishthana lay in the Deccan.

nc84f5be92ca.s: The account of the Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien is known as the:
nc84f5be92ca.x: Fa-Hien's account is the Fo-kwo-ki or Record of Buddhist Kingdoms; his main interest was Buddhism and he did not name the king.

n11eba5990ff.s: The 'urban decay' interpretation of the post-Gupta period is associated with:
n11eba5990ff.x: R.S. Sharma's urban decay thesis links shrinking towns, rural self-sufficiency and scarce gold coins.

nf14da17761a.s: According to Fa-Hien, free hospitals existed at:
nf14da17761a.x: Fa-Hien noted free hospitals at Pataliputra, 20 viharas at Mathura and decay at Kapilavastu, Gaya and Kushinagar.

n3fc754a21d3.s: Ghantasala and Kadura, ports of the Gupta period, were located in:
n3fc754a21d3.x: Ghantasala and Kadura were in Krishna district, while Kalyan and Chaul were on the Konkan coast.

n51e1de6bb00.s: The Narada Smriti lists how many types of slaves?
n51e1de6bb00.x: The Narada Smriti lists 15 types of slaves; Chandalas lived outside the varnas and settlements.

nad5593e9b90.s: In the Gupta period, Vidisha was noted for:
nad5593e9b90.x: Vidisha was known for cloth and ivory work; silk weaving was at Lata and Mandsaur.

nee1385d07ef.s: According to Fa-Hien, the Chandalas announced their approach by:
nee1385d07ef.x: Fa-Hien noted that Chandalas lived outside villages and towns and struck wood to warn others.

n0368593c068.s: The decline of trade in North India after the Guptas reduced the inflow of:
n0368593c068.x: Losing the north-western route and western India cut trade revenue and the inflow of gold and silver.

n9d77881194b.s: For their protection, some Gupta-period guilds maintained:
n9d77881194b.x: Some guilds had their own armed bodies (APPSC G1 2023 key); guild charity built temples, rest houses, halls and gardens.

n3b34289e194.s: In the Gupta period, women controlled their stridhana, which consisted of:
n3b34289e194.x: Women lacked general property rights but controlled stridhana, their marriage gifts.

n0672d971d25.x: Chinansuka means Chinese silk and shows the growth of trade with China.

n92cd937a0c3.s: The Gupta rupaka was a coin made of:
n92cd937a0c3.x: The rupaka was a silver coin issued after the conquest of the Western Satraps; gold dinaras were issued in the largest numbers.

n6a737b2b5d2.s: The Dashpur (Mandsaur) inscription, called the oldest advertisement in the Indian tradition, was composed by:
n6a737b2b5d2.x: The Dashpur inscription was composed by Vatsabhatti, not Bhava (the MPPSC trap).

n5447a65466b.s: In the Gupta period, the head of a guild was called the:
n5447a65466b.x: The head of a guild was the Sreshthi or Setti; a Sarthavaha was a caravan trader in long-distance trade.

nfd19bb59f75.s: Indian trade with the Eastern Roman Empire continued until about:
nfd19bb59f75.x: Eastern Roman trade continued until about 550 CE, before the post-Gupta decline and the stagnation of c. 750-1000 CE.

n2a30e6cb904.s: During the Gupta period, castes multiplied into numerous sub-castes mainly because:
o: foreigners and tribes were absorbed into the caste structure
Chandalas were admitted into the four varnas
n2a30e6cb904.x: Foreigners and tribes absorbed into the caste structure, particularly through land grants, multiplied the jatis.

n5a0abda1f04.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the stages carry no dates)
n5a0abda1f04.s: Which temple belongs to the first stage of Gupta temple architecture, with a flat roof and shallow four-pillared portico?
n5a0abda1f04.x: First-stage temples such as Sanchi Temple 17 and Tigawa had a square sanctum, flat roof and shallow portico; Nachna is second stage and Deogarh and Bhitargaon third.

n7df39cd9aa0.s: The Ajivika sect is associated with:
n7df39cd9aa0.x: Ajivika is associated with Makkhali Gosala; Jainism with Mahavira and Buddhism with Gautama Buddha.

nce7a2d41d0b.s: Tantrism, open to women and Shudras, began to spread from about which century CE?
nce7a2d41d0b.x: Tantrism spread from about the fifth century, centred on shakti, and influenced Shaivism, Vaishnavism, Buddhism and Jainism.

n90bbd429e0b.s: Amrakardava, who recorded a grant to a Buddhist vihara at Sanchi, was an officer of:
n90bbd429e0b.x: Amrakardava, an officer of Chandragupta II, recorded the Sanchi grant; the Kahaum pillar of Skandagupta's time records Jain images.

n3cdd42f2562.s: Compared with the Mauryan period, Gupta-age religious emphasis shifted from sacrifice to:
n3cdd42f2562.x: The Gupta shift was from sacrifice to temple worship and bhakti; the age is also called the Golden Age of art.

nca2e2cccc32.x: Buddhaghosa wrote the Visuddhimagga; Vasubandhu wrote the Abhidharmakosa and Dinnaga founded Buddhist logic.

n68fb79f0cb1.s: Buddhism in the Gupta period was persecuted by the Huna ruler:
n68fb79f0cb1.x: Buddhism lost royal patronage and was persecuted by Mihirakula, though Mahayana images flourished in Gupta art.

ncac5e319d69.s: The chakra, shankha and Garuda are symbols associated with:
ncac5e319d69.x: Chakra, shankha and Garuda belong to Vaishnavism; the linga to Saivism.

n29e97ada736.x: The Guptas patronised Bhagavatism, yet Samudragupta allowed Meghavarman to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya.

ne9d543a274a.s: Heliodorus, who set up the Garuda pillar at Besnagar, was the envoy of the Indo-Greek king:
ne9d543a274a.x: Heliodorus, envoy of Antialcidas at the court of the Sunga ruler Bhagabhadra, set up the Garuda pillar to Vasudeva.

ncb8b142639a.s: Bhagavatism centred on the worship of Vasudeva-Krishna of which clan?
ncb8b142639a.x: Bhagavatism centred on Vasudeva-Krishna of the Vrishni (Satvata) clan; its foundations were karma, bhakti and ahimsa.

nindian-history-51-32.s: The Lingayat sect followed the teachings of:
nindian-history-51-32.x: Lingayats followed Basava; Pashupata was founded by Lakulisha and the Nathpanth led by Matsyendranath and Gorakhnath.

nfe03e963530.s: The Pashupata sect, the oldest Shaiva sect, was founded by:
nfe03e963530.x: Pashupata, the oldest Shaiva sect, was founded by Lakulisha (Nakulisha); in it pashu is the individual soul and pati the Supreme soul.

n97cf2c68989.s: The earliest example of the Panchayatana plan is the:
n97cf2c68989.x: The Panchayatana plan (main shrine plus four corner shrines) first appears at the Deogarh Dashavatara temple; Bhumara has only two flanking shrines.

n46c1d1c144d.s: The raised platform on which Gupta temples stood is called the:
n46c1d1c144d.x: Gupta temples established the square garbhagriha, pillared mandapa, pradakshina path and raised jagati platform.

n347ad7499e0.s: The Gupta-period Sultanganj Buddha, more than two metres high, is made of:
n347ad7499e0.x: The Sultanganj Buddha is a bronze image more than two metres high; Gupta stone sculpture grew out of the Mathura school.

n1a19e964f87.s: Which Gupta temple has two flanking shrines at the entrance?
n1a19e964f87.x: Bhumara has flanking shrines; Sanchi 17 a flat roof, Nachna a covered ambulatory and Deogarh a shikhara with panchayatana plan.

n8e2a14b1c8d.x: The Aryabhatiya was composed in 499 CE; it held the Earth spherical and rotating and gave an accurate value of pi.

n4c3bc2c4f91.s: The peak of Sanskrit literature, Ajanta painting and Sarnath sculpture are cited to call which period a 'Classical' age?
n4c3bc2c4f91.x: These, along with advances in mathematics and astronomy and the first structural temples, are grounds for calling the Gupta period classical.

n4a311fbca76.s: Which of the following is cited as a criticism of calling the Gupta period a 'Golden Age'?
o: Expansion of vishti or forced labour
n4a311fbca76.x: Growth of land grants and feudatories, expansion of vishti, decline of trade and towns and the falling status of women are cited against the label.

n7fc0a916f6f.s: The Gwalior inscription showing zero as a circle is dated:
n7fc0a916f6f.x: The Gwalior inscription of 876 CE shows zero as a circle; the Mankani plates (AD 595-596) are cited as the earliest epigraphic place-value use.

n0570ef0035a.s: How many Buddhist viharas were there at Bagh?
n0570ef0035a.x: Bagh had nine Buddhist viharas, not five.

nd61f819b8d0.s: Harishena's Prayaga Prashasti records the achievements of:
nd61f819b8d0.x: The Prayaga Prashasti records Samudragupta's achievements; the Harishena of the Brihatkatha Kosha was a different, later Jain author.

n629dd9c3776.s: The Katantra grammar was written by:
n629dd9c3776.x: Sharvavarman wrote the Katantra; Amarasimha the Amarakosha, Chandragomin the Chandra Vyakarana and Vararuchi the Prakrit Prakasha.

n8fa1503f9a6.s: The Romaka and Paulisa Siddhantas show which influence on Gupta-age science?
n8fa1503f9a6.x: The Romaka and Paulisa Siddhantas show Greek input into Indian science.

nf93fe528d64.s: The Mehrauli iron pillar was originally set up at:
nf93fe528d64.x: The pillar, now at Mehrauli in Delhi, was originally erected at Udayagiri near Vidisha.

nf34c22e229f.s: The Gupta-period Udayagiri caves, with Varaha and Shiva images, are located near:
nf34c22e229f.x: The Udayagiri caves near Vidisha in Madhya Pradesh comprise twenty caves, nineteen Hindu and one Jain.

ndc2a9ee6d7d.s: The Hitopadesha was a later work based on the:
ndc2a9ee6d7d.x: The Hitopadesha was composed later and was based on the Panchatantra.

nbf58c2cf432.s: In technique, the Ajanta paintings are:
o: tempera on dry lime plaster (fresco secco)
nbf58c2cf432.x: Ajanta paintings are tempera on dry lime plaster, not true fresco; outlines were first drawn in red and then filled.

n75944ad1c1d.s: At Ajanta, the Mother and Child panel is associated with Cave:
n75944ad1c1d.x: The Mother and Child panel is in Cave 17; Padmapani and Vajrapani are Bodhisattvas.

ncf91a1ecc96.x: Hastyayurveda was written by Palakapya, not Dhanvantari.

ne910800832a.s: Vetala Bhatta, of the Gupta age, is associated with:
ne910800832a.x: Vetala Bhatta is associated with Mantrashastra; Dhanvantari with Ayurveda and Vararuchi with Prakrit grammar.

ne6109963735.s: Navanitakam was an ancient medical manual dealing with:
ne6109963735.x: Navanitakam dealt with metallic preparations; physicians used iron and mercury preparations and performed lithotomy.

nindian-history-6-34.s: The Geet Govind dates to which century?
nindian-history-6-34.x: The Geet Govind dates to the 12th century.

n7613ee958fe.x: Shudraka wrote the Mrichchhakatika; Bhasa wrote Charudatta and Vishakhadatta the Devichandraguptam.

n7f50a8a8cfe.s: The Veena-player (lyrist) type of Gupta gold coin was issued by:
n7f50a8a8cfe.x: The lyrist type belongs to Samudragupta; archer and lion-slayer types to Chandragupta II and the king feeding peacock type to Kumaragupta I.

n8e8043aa7fa.x: Lilavati is by Bhaskara II (12th century); Bhaskara I wrote a commentary on the Aryabhatiya.

nindian-history-48-10.s: Chandapradyota of Avanti was treated by the physician:
nindian-history-48-10.x: Jivaka, physician of Bimbisara, treated Chandapradyota of Avanti, not Sushruta.

necab90582e6.s: The later phase of Ajanta was patronised by the Vakataka king:
necab90582e6.x: Ajanta's later phase was patronised by the Vakataka king Harishena; the earliest paintings are in Caves 9 and 10.

nc45ce0fa426.x: The Brahmasphutasiddhanta is by Brahmagupta; Varahamihira wrote the Panchasiddhantika, Brihat Samhita and Brihat Jataka.

nindian-history-14-12.s: Which Srivijaya king endowed a monastery at Nalanda?
nindian-history-14-12.x: Balaputradeva of Srivijaya endowed a monastery at Nalanda, which drew students from China, Tibet, Korea and Srivijaya.

nindian-history-12-6.s: The largest hoard of Gupta coins was found at:
nindian-history-12-6.x: The largest Gupta hoard was found at Bayana in Bharatpur, Rajasthan.

nindian-history-13-11.s: The Sanskrit drama Malavikagnimitram was written by:
nindian-history-13-11.x: Kalidasa wrote the drama Malavikagnimitram and the poems Meghaduta and Kumarasambhavam.

nindian-history-13-12.s: The Buddhacharita and the Saundarananda were written by:
nindian-history-13-12.x: Ashvaghosha wrote the Buddhacharita, on the life of the Buddha, and the Saundarananda.

nb2eaf23e2a7.s: Which cave site in Andhra Pradesh is known for five caves and a Nataraja image?
nb2eaf23e2a7.x: Mogalrajapuram has five caves and a Nataraja image; Bhairavakonda has eight Kapalika caves.

n694807a30ee.s: Varahamihira, listed in the traditional Navaratna of Chandragupta II, actually belonged to which century?
n694807a30ee.x: The Navaratna list is traditional; Varahamihira belonged to the sixth century, later than Chandragupta II.

nindian-history-6-33.s: The Sanskrit drama Svapnavasavadattam was written by:

n1f71440c5de.s: Which of the following is one of the five siddhantas summarised in Varahamihira's Panchasiddhantika?
n1f71440c5de.x: The five are Surya, Romaka, Paulisa, Vasishtha and Paitamaha.

neb3c6808db2.s: Sarnath school Gupta sculptures were made of polished:
neb3c6808db2.x: Sarnath sculpture used polished Chunar buff sandstone and avoided heavy ornamentation.

n94b35c144a4.s: In the traditional Navaratna list, Kshapanaka is associated with:
n94b35c144a4.x: Kshapanaka is linked with Jyotishyashastra; Shanku with architecture, Dhanvantari with Ayurveda and Amarasimha with the Amarakosha.

n6c5f24eaea7.s: Which inscription bears the signature of Harsha?
n6c5f24eaea7.x: The Banskhera inscription bears Harsha's signature; the Madhuban plate is a land-grant record useful for chronology.

n4d7204ae644.s: Harsha's Prayag assembly was held every:
n4d7204ae644.x: The Prayag assembly was held every five years; Hiuen Tsang attended the sixth, where Harsha gave away his treasury.

nindian-history-45-20.x: Hastimalla was a Kannada poet and playwright; Kshemendra was the Kashmiri poet and Kalidasa Chandragupta II's court poet.

n7c7220ab12f.s: According to Hiuen Tsang, the economy of Harsha's time showed:
o: decline of trade and a self-sufficient agrarian economy
n7c7220ab12f.x: Hiuen Tsang saw a decline of trade and the rise of a self-sufficient agrarian economy; taxes were not heavy.

nindian-history-144-7.x: The Mahamoksha Council met at the Prayagraj Sangam; the Kannauj Assembly drew rulers of 20 countries.

nindian-history-144-12.s: Harsha was defeated by Pulakesin II on the banks of the:
nindian-history-144-12.x: Harsha was defeated by Pulakesin II on the Narmada.

nindian-history-46-5.x: Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita and Kadambari.

nf616454ef6a.x: Grahavarman was a Maukhari; Sasanka ruled Gauda, Bhaskaravarman Kamarupa and Dhruvasena II Valabhi.

n278fba82702.s: Hiuen Tsang described which city as a Gurjara capital?
n278fba82702.x: Hiuen Tsang described Bhinmal as a Gurjara capital and mentioned the Sun temple of Multan.

nad82bbdd4ec.s: Which record is useful for establishing the chronology of Harsha's reign?
nad82bbdd4ec.x: The Madhuban plate is useful for Harsha's chronology, alongside the Sonpat seal and the Banskhera inscription.

n3efe87dd6ec.x: The Harsha era began in 606 CE, the year of his accession; 647 CE is the year of his death.

nc7e4c64d18f.s: Prabhavatigupta's regency in the Vakataka kingdom gave the Guptas indirect control of the:
nc7e4c64d18f.x: Prabhavatigupta, daughter of Chandragupta II and wife of Rudrasena II, gave the Guptas indirect control of the Deccan as regent.

n775756f31e2.s: In Harsha's time, Nalanda was headed by:
n775756f31e2.x: Nalanda, founded by Kumaragupta I, was headed by Silabhadra in Harsha's time.

ne86f0790d97.s: According to Hiuen Tsang, Dhanyakataka had about 20 viharas of which sect?
ne86f0790d97.x: Dhanyakataka had about 20 Mahasanghika viharas and Vengi about 20 viharas; Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda were decaying.

nindian-history-46-32.x: Rajasekhara wrote the Viddhasalabhanjika; Bhavabhuti wrote the Mahaviracharitam.

nae1ca339f29.x: Harsha's titles were Siladitya and Sakalottarapathanatha; he died in 647 CE without an heir.

n9ee43865a1c.s: In Harsha's administration, Simhanada was the:
n9ee43865a1c.x: Simhanada was commander-in-chief; Avanti handled war and peace, Kuntala the cavalry and Skandagupta the elephant force.

nf2ef6234500.s: The Kannauj assembly held to honour Hiuen Tsang lasted for:
nf2ef6234500.x: The Kannauj assembly honoured Hiuen Tsang, propagated Mahayana and lasted 23 days; it was followed by violence and an attempt on Harsha's life.

n1230d26c9f4.s: The only Vakataka ruler to assume the title Samrat was:
n1230d26c9f4.x: Pravarasena I, son of Vindhyashakti, was the only Vakataka Samrat and performed the Vajapeya and Ashvamedha.

n82e47be7834.s: Nalanda provided free boarding for about how many students?
n82e47be7834.x: Nalanda accommodated about 10,000 students with free boarding; Hiuen Tsang studied and taught there.

nb9c6a4307ed.s: Which of the following was a pro-Buddhist measure of Harsha?
nb9c6a4307ed.x: Harsha banned animal food and punished the killing of living beings, while continuing to patronise Brahmanical scholars.

n5fe371a943f.s: The capital of Shashanka, Harsha's rival in Gauda, was:
n5fe371a943f.x: Shashanka's capital was Karnasuvarna; Harsha allied with Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa against him.

n63f3a09d1f7.s: Besides Harsha and Pulakesin II, Hiuen Tsang praised which Pallava ruler?
n63f3a09d1f7.x: Hiuen Tsang praised Harsha, Pulakesin II of the Chalukyas and Narasimhavarman of the Pallavas.

nindian-history-46-24.s: Rajasekhara, court scholar of the Gurjara-Pratiharas, wrote the:
nindian-history-46-24.x: Rajasekhara, at the court of Mahendrapala I and Mahipala I, wrote the Kavyamimamsa; Tarikh-i-Subuktigin is by Baihaqi.

nindian-history-46-7.s: The Mattavilasa Prahasana was written by:
nindian-history-46-7.x: Mattavilasa Prahasana is by the Pallava king Mahendravarman I; Dandin wrote Dashakumaracharita and Bharavi Kiratarjuniyam.

nindian-history-144-6.s: Harsha's Kannauj Assembly, attended by rulers of 20 countries, was held in:
nindian-history-144-6.x: The Kannauj Assembly of 643 AD was attended by rulers of 20 countries, Brahmins, Shramanas and courtiers.

nf54db66fcc4.s: Dhruvasena II of Valabhi became Harsha's vassal and married Harsha's:
nf54db66fcc4.x: Dhruvasena II of Valabhi was made Harsha's vassal and married Harsha's daughter.

n28ff6d4c52e.s: According to Hiuen Tsang, which Andhra vihara suffered from lack of patronage?
n28ff6d4c52e.x: Hiuen Tsang recorded lack of patronage at Sriparvata vihara and decay at Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda.

naea473f4643.s: Kannauj, to which Harsha later shifted his capital from Thanesar, was earlier the capital of the:
naea473f4643.x: Thanesar was Harsha's first capital; Kannauj was the Maukhari capital, to which he later shifted.

n8da16121717.s: Under Harsha, the state revenue was divided into how many parts?
n8da16121717.x: Revenue was divided four ways: the king's use, public servants, scholars and religious activities.

nindian-history-1-91.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the tripartite struggle for Kannauj?
o: Govinda III was a Rashtrakuta king.
The Sanjan and Radhanpur plates record Govinda III's northern victories.
Nagabhata II, defeated by Govinda III, was a Pala king.
The Khalimpur inscription records the election of Gopala.
nindian-history-1-91.x: Nagabhata II was a Gurjara-Pratihara king, not a Pala; the other three statements are correct.

ndd9f13a702a.s: Access to Arabian Sea trade through Gujarat let the masters of Kannauj bypass the Arab-held:
ndd9f13a702a.x: Kannauj commanded the Doab's agrarian wealth and Arabian Sea trade via Gujarat, bypassing the Arab-held Indus delta.

n17a8bc4c8d8.s: The capital of the Rashtrakutas during the tripartite struggle was:
n17a8bc4c8d8.x: The Rashtrakuta capital was Manyakheta (Malkhed) in the Deccan; the Pratiharas later held Kannauj.

n228624951fd.s: Which Rashtrakuta ruler defeated both Vatsaraja and Dharmapala but returned south with booty?
n228624951fd.x: Dhruva defeated Vatsaraja and Dharmapala, took booty and returned south without retaining northern territory.

n550c3c502d7.s: Whom did Dharmapala install as ruler of Kannauj?
n550c3c502d7.x: Dharmapala installed Chakrayudha at Kannauj after Vatsaraja's occupation; Nagabhata II later ousted him.

n08592ade6f0.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates)
n08592ade6f0.s: Which Pala ruler founded both Vikramashila and Somapura?
n08592ade6f0.x: Dharmapala founded Vikramashila and Somapura; Gopala built Odantapuri and Nalanda was founded by Kumaragupta I.

ncb520c34425.s: Vikramashila Mahavihara, at Antichak, lies in which district of Bihar?
ncb520c34425.x: Vikramashila is at Antichak in Bhagalpur district, not Banka (BPSC 2023 trap).

n2445a738333.s: The Kaivarta revolt took place in the reign of the Pala ruler:
n2445a738333.x: Ramapala (c. 1072-1126), the last strong Pala ruler, faced the Kaivarta revolt and is associated with Jagaddala.

n4b2e78af92f.s: Dharmapala was defeated by Nagabhata II near:
n4b2e78af92f.x: Dharmapala (c. 770-810) was defeated by Dhruva and by Nagabhata II near Monghyr.

n08dec664b90.s: The Pala founder Gopala displaced the Khadgas of:
n08dec664b90.x: Gopala displaced the later Guptas in Magadha and the Khadgas in eastern Bengal, and built Odantapuri.

nindian-history-14-11.s: Nalanda University in Bihar was founded in which century AD?
nindian-history-14-11.x: Nalanda was founded in the 5th century AD by the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I.

na0c30f11f9e.s: Under the Palas, which centre became associated with translating books into Tibetan?
na0c30f11f9e.x: Jagaddala was associated with translations into Tibetan, while Buddhist texts were compiled at Nalanda under Dharmapala.

n543271d8c2c.s: Illustrated Buddhist manuscripts of the Pala period were written on:
n543271d8c2c.x: Pala art includes bronze and black-stone sculpture and illustrated palm-leaf Buddhist manuscripts.

n1eb8e44ceef.s: In the time of Harsha, Valabhi was known as a centre of:
n1eb8e44ceef.x: Valabhi was a Hinayana centre in Harsha's time, distinct from the Pala Mahaviharas.
